rule: Maximum acceptable in-session pain: 2/10 (validator/readiness threshold mirroring the ladder pain rule)
summary: Trials of pain-monitoring models accept up to 5/10 with next-morning return to baseline (Silbernagel 2007; Sprague 2021), and meta-analyses find no harm from painful exercise (Smith 2017; Tran 2025): 2/10 is deliberately stricter, justified by the back/shoulder history. Safety rule: not loosened. Duplicates progressions.rules.regress_on_session_pain_above; keep the two equal (a check that they match would prevent drift).

sources.note: Silbernagel 2007 RCT (n=38, Achilles): continued running/jumping under a pain-monitoring model was no worse than 6 weeks of active rest
Pilot RCT (patellar tendinopathy): Pain-Monitoring Model = pain <= 5/10 during/after activity and back to pre-activity level by next morning; feasible, high compliance
Smith 2017 MA (7 RCTs, chronic MSK pain): painful exercise small short-term benefit vs pain-free, no difference medium/long term; pain need not be a barrier
Tran 2025 updated MA (16 RCTs): no difference painful vs non-painful exercise; very low-low certainty; pain may not need to be avoided
Farrar 2001 (2724 pts): ~2 points / ~30% on a 0-10 NRS is a clinically important change; smaller shifts sit within noise
